subject: Staged annual advance to hedge renewal increases
messages:
From: Emily Harper <e.harper@cloudscale.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal concern — upcoming rate increases and multi-year option

Jonas / Marissa,

Quick note from my side as we prep for the Oct renewal: our finance team is pushing hard to avoid sticker increases next year. CloudScale is very interested in a multi-year arrangement if it can lock rate stability, but they want flexibility on ramping usage (we expect a 2x growth over 12 months).

Key asks from procurement:
- Price protection across 24 months or a cap on per-token increases
- Ability to buy annual advance credits with a staged drawdown (we don’t want to prepay the total upfront)
- Ramp credits or true‑up terms if we exceed commit in year 1

Can you share structuring options and any sample term sheet? I attached our forecast so you can see expected ramp.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Harper
Head of Cloud Engineering, CloudScale
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Emily Harper <e.harper@cloudscale.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal concern — upcoming rate increases and multi-year option

Thanks Emily — appreciate the heads up and the forecast. Attached is a draft term-sheet that maps to three practical levers we typically offer to hedge rate risk while preserving ramp flexibility:

1) Staged Annual Advance (preferred):
   - Customer prepays the Year 1 and Year 2 committed spend in two annual installments (paid at start of each contract year).
   - Redwood commits to a rate cap for 24 months relative to the initial invoice rate.
   - If CloudScale exceeds the committed tokens in a year, overage is billed at a negotiated overage rate (lower than on-demand) and a portion converts into Year+1 credits.

2) Multi-year Prepay with Ramp Credits:
   - One upfront prepayment for 24 months with graduated refund/credit schedule if growth materially undershoots.
   - Higher headline discount for full prepay (typically 12–15% vs. 8–10% for staged).

3) Hybrid: Reserved GPU + Prepay Credits:
   - Combine dedicated capacity commitment for hot workloads with prepay credits for burst/variable usage.

Suggested numbers based on your forecast:
- Year 1 commit: $300k (10% discount vs. on-demand)
- Year 2 commit: $600k (8% discount)
- Overage: billed monthly at 60% of on-demand token price; cumulative overage >20% triggers an automatic top-up of Year 2 credits.

I’ve attached redwood-staged-prepay-term-sheet-v3.pdf and flagged the clauses you’ll likely negotiate (invoicing cadence, true‑up, audit window, early termination). If it sounds reasonable, I’ll loop in Finance for formal pricing approval and arrange a procurement call with your team.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-19T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: CloudScale — need finance signoff on staged prepay numbers

Folks — Emily sent their forecast. I proposed a staged annual advance structure (see email thread). They prefer not to prepay all at once but want a firm rate cap.

Questions for Finance (Ben):
- Can we accept the Year 1 / Year 2 discount cadence (10% / 8%) for this ARR profile?
- Confirm acceptable overage mechanics: monthly billing at 60% of on‑demand with a >20% cumulative threshold that converts to Year 2 credit.
- Any concerns on revenue recognition or refund windows if they undershoot?

Timelines: procurement wants a term sheet this week to present to execs on Monday. I can host a short call with Emily + procurement if needed.

Thanks — Jonas
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-19T15:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: CloudScale — need finance signoff on staged prepay numbers

Jonas — quick take from rev/finance:
- The 10% / 8% ladder is acceptable given the two-year locked pricing commitment; we can push to 11% for Year 1 if we want to be more competitive, but margin impact is modest.
- Overage at 60% on-demand is fine but add a cap (e.g., 1.5x of forecasted monthly on-peak) to avoid runaway exposure.
- Revenue recognition: staged annual payments recognized as deferred revenue over each contract year; make sure procurement accepts non-refundable language after each invoice (standard).

I’ll edit the term sheet with the cap language and a short true‑up example for procurement. Send me the final numbers and I’ll sign off.

-Ben
From: Emily Harper <e.harper@cloudscale.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: CloudScale Procurement <procurement@cloudscale.io>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-21T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal concern — upcoming rate increases and multi-year option

Jonas — thanks for the quick turnaround and Ben for the finance guidance. Procurement reviewed the draft term sheet and CloudScale is comfortable proceeding on the following:

Agreed high-level:
- Staged Annual Advance for 24 months (invoices at the start of each contract year).
- Year 1 committed spend: $300,000 (11% discount applied as Ben suggested).
- Year 2 committed spend: $600,000 (8% discount).
- Overage billed monthly at 60% of on-demand, with a hard cap at 1.5x forecasted peak month; cumulative overage above 20% will convert to Year 2 credits.
- Redwood guarantees a rate cap for 24 months relative to the Year 1 invoice rate.

Procurement asks to add a 30‑day review period in Year 1 to reconcile actuals and confirm Year 2 invoice amount (we want visibility before the second prepay). Also asked about audit right windows and a 90‑day notice for committing to Year 2 invoice in case there’s a strategic change.

If you can incorporate the 30‑day review and the 90‑day flexible notice into the term sheet, we’ll get internal signoff and return countersigned copy. I’ve attached our forecast again for reference.

Looking forward to closing this out — we view this as a good compromise between certainty and operational flexibility.

Best,
Emily
